items.prompt: Which tag defines the most important heading on a page?

explanation.whyCorrect: <h1> is the top-level heading — the single most important one on the page.
whyOthersWrong: <h6> is the smallest heading, not the largest.
<head> holds metadata and is not visible on the page.
<title> sets the browser-tab text, not an on-page heading.
explanation.bestPractice: Use exactly one <h1> per page to name its main topic.

items.prompt: Select ALL valid HTML heading tags.

explanation.whyCorrect: HTML defines six heading levels, h1 through h6, so <h1> and <h3> are both valid.
whyOthersWrong: <h7> does not exist — headings stop at h6.
<heading> is not a real HTML tag.
explanation.bestPractice: Don't skip levels: move h1 to h2 to h3 in order.

items.prompt: To create the largest heading, you use the ____ tag. Write just the tag name.

explanation.whyCorrect: The <h1> tag creates the largest, most important heading.
explanation.bestPractice: Reserve <h1> for the page's main title.

items.prompt: By default, how will a browser display the text 'Hello' here?

explanation.whyCorrect: Browsers render <h1> text large and bold by default.
whyOthersWrong: Small and faint describes muted text or lower-level headings, not <h1>.
A clickable link requires an <a> tag.
explanation.bestPractice: Appearance is the job of CSS — choose a heading level for meaning, not size.
